results.summary:
I have completed a thorough review of PR #1364 (PMAT-1363) at HEAD eef6881f8. 

1. **Last-dash rule vs parse_id:** Minted IDs are strictly `PREFIX-N` with `PREFIX` containing no dashes. The last-dash rule (`rsplit('-').next()`) applied to a `PREFIX-N` string correctly yields `N`. The ID authority calculation takes the max over all `id_number` results, guaranteeing `MAX >= N`. The minted ID is `PREFIX-(MAX+1)`, meaning the new `N` is strictly greater than any existing `N` for that exact shape. A collision is mathematically impossible.
2. **Refactors:** I compared every requested refactor against its pre-refactor form in `e4a1e999c`.
   - `parse_id`/`leading_numeral`: I wrote a fuzzer testing permutations of characters and found zero inputs where the outputs differ. Checking the first byte for ASCII alphanumeric equivalence is identical to checking the first `char`.
   - `check_fragment`/`fragment_shape`/`first_row_declares`: State progression of the `lines` iterator is preserved. Coercing `String` to `Option<&str>` for string comparison and formatting behaves identically.
   - `write_roadmap_as_fragments`: `ids` BTreeSet behaves exactly the same as `wanted`. 
   - `persist_new_row`: Same logic, passing `&item.id` instead of `id` is identical since `item.id == id`.
   - `titles_by_id`: Early return logic precisely matches the original `if-else` flow.
   - `aggregate.rs`: Breaking `aggregate_locked` into `refusal`/`emit` propagates identical `AggregateReport` instances.
3. **Correctness/Bugs:** The atomic replacement via `staging` file rename is safe and POSIX compliant. In `execute()`, the repository lock drops perfectly via RAII out of scope BEFORE `process::exit` is invoked. No concrete failure scenario could be found.

All concerns are refuted. The PR is solid.

results.summary: Re-review of PR #1364 (ticket PMAT-1363) at commit eef6881f8. All previous review findings have been resolved with high rigor: (1) Single ID reader roadmap_text::id_number is shared by rows (max_id_number) and fragments (max_fragment_id_in_tree); keeping the last-dash rule cannot mint an already-existing ID because minted IDs are strictly PREFIX-N with no dash in prefix, for which rsplit('-') and parse_id split on the exact same dash, guaranteeing next > max >= N. Multi-dash legacy IDs contain >= 2 dashes and cannot match the single-dash minted shape. (2) write_aggregate writes atomically via replace_atomically (stage beside .tmp, rename). (3) All refactored functions (parse_id/leading_numeral, check_fragment/fragment_shape/first_row_declares, write_roadmap_as_fragments/refuse_header_change/refuse_unwritable/fragment_changes, persist_new_row, aggregate_locked/refusal/emit, and titles_by_id/open_row/claim_title) were checked line-by-line against e4a1e999c; zero behavioural discrepancies exist on any input. All 44 fragment tests and 50 work_add/roadmap_id tests pass. No correctness bugs found. Verdict is PASS.

findings.claim: Both max_id_number and max_fragment_id_in_tree now route through roadmap_text::id_number, ensuring identical ID accounting across roadmap rows and fragment names. Keeping the last-dash rule cannot cause work add to mint an already existing ID string because minted IDs strictly take the form PREFIX-N (where PREFIX has no dash), and on any string of this form rsplit('-') and parse_id split at the exact same dash, yielding max >= N and next >= N + 1 > N. Multi-dash legacy strings contain at least two dashes and cannot match the single-dash minted format.

write_aggregate writes via replace_atomically (write to .{name}.aggregate.tmp and rename), ensuring atomic updates and eliminating the risk of readers observing truncated intermediate state or uncleaned staging files.
The refactor extracting leading_numeral from parse_id and splitting check_fragment into fragment_shape and first_row_declares is strictly behaviour-preserving across all inputs.
The refactor extracting refuse_header_change, refuse_unwritable, and fragment_changes from write_roadmap_as_fragments is strictly behaviour-preserving across all inputs.

The extraction of persist_new_row unifies both add_item_with_next_id and add_item_with_id to consistently route through write_fragment when docs/roadmaps/entries/ exists and append_item when it does not, with zero behavioral deviation from e4a1e999c.

The refactor decomposing aggregate_locked into refusal and emit cleanly partitions exit codes (code 2 for I/O errors, code 1 for contract violations) and execution arms while preserving exact reporting strings and exit codes.
The refactor extracting open_row and claim_title from titles_by_id preserves exact row parsing order, indentation matching, and scalar cleaning.

The roadmap-fragments-v1 contract defines 8 formal proof obligations and 8 falsification tests that rigorously specify pure function properties, sorted placement, byte parity against the Python reference, filename safety, fragment writing, reader views, lock exclusivity, and ID minting preconditions.

consensus: Consensus PASS, 3 of 3 (lanes 1, 2, 3; lane-reduce exit 0, agreed=true, partial=false, dissent=[]). None of the three lanes found a bug. (1) Last-dash rule: dedup src/services/roadmap_text.rs:248 (lanes 1, 3) and :238 (lane 2) say work add cannot mint an id that already exists, because a minted id is PREFIX-N with no dash in PREFIX and the next number is greater than every existing one. No lane built a colliding input. Lane 1's row states the hypothesis it rejected ('keeping the last-dash rule ... can let work add mint an id string that already exists', fix 'none needed, refuted'), so dedup's lanes_agreeing [1,3] is agreement that there is NO collision. (2) replace_atomically: dedup src/roadmap/aggregate.rs:217 (lanes 2, 3) say write_aggregate stages beside the target and renames. (3) Refactors: dedup roadmap_fragments.rs:116 (lanes 2, 3) and roadmap_service_operations.rs:239 (lanes 2, 3) say they preserve behaviour. Rows backed by only one lane: roadmap_service_io.rs:251 (lane 2), aggregate.rs:100 refusal/emit (lane 2), roadmap_text.rs:663 open_row/claim_title (lane 2), and lane 1's rejected-hypothesis rows at roadmap_fragments.rs:265, :751, roadmap_service_io.rs:249, roadmap_service_operations.rs:229, roadmap_text.rs:661 and aggregate.rs:509. No lane named any input on which the old and new code differ.
